H7225.entry:
From the same as H7218; the first, in place, time, order or rank (specifically, a firstfruit).

Used of the beginning of time (Genesis 1:1), the first of a series, the best or choicest portion of something (as in the firstfruits offered to God), or the chief or principal part.

Commonly translated as: beginning, first, firstfruits, best, chief, choice, principal, former.

H430.entry:
Plural of H433; gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God.

Occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative. The plural form with singular meaning when referring to the God of Israel is often called the 'plural of majesty' or 'plural of intensity.'

Commonly translated as: God, god, gods, judge, angels, exceeding, great, mighty, very.

G2316.entry:
Of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with G3588) the supreme Divinity.

Figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very. In the New Testament it refers almost exclusively to the one true God, the Father, and occasionally to Christ or the Holy Spirit as sharing the divine nature.

Commonly translated as: God, god, godly, good-god-ward (speech).
